name: shoulder bones and joints overview
title: Shoulder bone and joint problems: AC joint separation versus AC osteoarthritis by onset; glenohumeral arthritis split by passive motion and cuff strength into noninflammatory and inflammatory; instability split by trauma into traumatic and atraumatic; and adhesive capsulitis with global stiffness and a normal X-ray; each with presentation, examination and X-ray, and treatment in order

root.title: Shoulder bones and joints: WHERE is it, and is PASSIVE motion lost too?
lines: acute injury = AC instability · gradual = arthritis · stiff with a normal X-ray, no trauma = adhesive capsulitis
always conservative first: surgery only once it is exhausted · rotator cuff disease (active motion << passive) is on the MUSCLES OF THE SHOULDER chart

head: h
Atraumatic
'born loose' · AMBRI
pres: case: a dozen dislocations, both shoulders, pops out on its own → physiotherapy
inv: ? connective tissue disorder · ? poor motor control

head: h
Adhesive capsulitis
2% of adults · 20% of diabetics · 40s–50s
mostly idiopathic
pres: • with diabetes, cervical disc, thyroid, cardiac disease
case: 47, diabetic, 4 months of pain, progressive loss of motion
inv: rules out arthritis and post-traumatic deformity
tx: beats physiotherapy, same by 1 year · or hydrodistension

panels.title: Stiff shoulder: causes and stages
items: intra-articular: arthritis, post-traumatic deformity · extra-articular: capsular, muscular, heterotopic bone · combined

panels.title: What keeps the head centred
items: ligaments + labrum matter most · bones · rotator cuff · nerves
labrum: more surface area, more depth, bumper effect
reduced → subluxated → dislocated is a continuum
diagnose by onset (traumatic or not) · direction (anterior, posterior, inferior) · degree
